systems_note: SDR receivers feed Home Assistant through rtl_433, a community add-on rather than an official integration. Broadlink and Tuya hubs have official Home Assistant integrations.

awards.label: Best SDR Receiver
awards.why: The standard rtl_433 stick, with a 1 PPM TCXO and a dipole antenna kit, and 6,497 reviews.

awards.label: Best Budget SDR
awards.why: The same RTL-SDR Blog V3 without the antenna kit, for $37.95, rated 4.6 stars.

awards.label: Best RF Bridge
awards.why: Learns 433 MHz fixed-code remotes and IR, with Alexa, Google, and an official Home Assistant integration.

awards.label: Best Premium SDR
awards.why: Nooelec's v5 with a 0.5 PPM TCXO and better HF, VHF, and UHF noise performance than a V3, per Nooelec.

specs.extras: 1 PPM TCXO, bias tee, dipole kit

products.verdict: A Smart Life IR/RF hub that's clear about what it can't do: fixed-code 433.92 MHz only.

avoid.flag: Promises garage doors without the rolling-code caveat
avoid.verdict: It lists garage doors as a use, but never mentions that rolling-code garage remotes can't be copied, which the other RF hubs here state plainly.
reasons: Garage doors are named in the title and bullets, with no mention of rolling codes.
BroadLink and Toyanc both say rolling-code devices aren't supported, and most garage remotes made in the last 25 years use rolling codes.
RF devices don't support voice control, per its own last bullet.
3.1 stars, the lowest of the RF hubs here.
